100k wide: completed 24.4 s, 100,000 entries once, 1 pass, 888-byte progress, 54 MB in-process peak, 12.3 s publication. 100k fan-out: completed 37.5 s, window <= 64 cursors, 99,873 durable rows, 6.8 KB progress, 52 MB peak. 1M wide (cap 4 GiB): completed 506.6 s, 1,000,000 entries once, 90 MB in-process peak, 150.6 s publication with 2.98 GB WAL peak and a 3.3 GB final database (storage amplification handed to TASK-532). Rows and supervision in scale-runs/.

discovered_risks: Publication remains one atomic reconciliation transaction; WAL growth at one million files is measured, not bounded, pending TASK-532 headroom accounting.
Continuation is cooperative wall-time budgeting; a slow filesystem call is not preempted. The stall detector reports lack of progress without diagnosing its cause.
Directories larger than 512 names stream in native order; lexical order is preserved only for directories that fit one retained read.
Stream eviction beyond 64 concurrently open passes restarts the evicted passes; very wide fan-in of active roots repeats work.
Scale evidence is a supervised synthetic workload on one machine, not an installed-app or overnight run.
